reviews.review: When i bought this game, i'm not sure is it worth this price tag. But after i played with for a while, i know this game is worth my money. The graphic and game physics were upgraded to a new level than the previous version. And the gameplay still remain unchanged , which is blow everything away LOL. And the new weapon system gives some fresh air into the game , making weapons  can be upgrade make you feel less frustrated when you keep getting the same weapon. Lastly, the brand new story and monster was awesome to watch and fight and it is much harder than the EDF 4.1 , so i will suggest find some friends to play together and saving the Earth ! EDF!! EDF!!!!!!!

EDF 5 brings some major improvements over its predecessor, but it also manages to take a few steps back in some areas.

The Good:
 - Weapons can be leveled up when duplicates are obtained, thus having use even at higher missions.
 - Armor and weapon pickups affect all classes.  No more having to grind each class separately, though the one you play has a higher chance of receiving the upgrade.
 - All classes can now heal their subordinates, not just the Ranger.
 - All classes have major upgrades, including special gear that give them special perks, as well as now having a pickup radius while performing dashes (or in a vehicle).
 - Rangers have access to vehicles or special gear that can do things such as increase healing abilities or pickup radius.
 - Wing Divers have an evasive dash and access to Cores that tweak their flying abilities.
 - Air Raiders have an extra weapon slot, and are less reliant on kill points and other units/players.  Some air strikes have a cooldown timer, instead that reload even when not equipped.  
 - Fencers can equip two special perks, such as doubling a shield's durability or performing multiple dashes/jumps.
 - The music is great.  Actually like it a bit more than 4.

The Bad:
 - EDF 4: "I have the cheesiest dialogue of any game!"
   EDF 5: "Hold my beer...  'We have to get to the ground surface!'"
 - "To save our Mother Earth from any ali--- wait.  What the hell is this?"
    They replaced the memorable cadences of 4 with something much less memorable.  Unfortunately, the NPC soldiers love to sing them far too often.
 - Some vehicle controls, like the motorcycles and Depth Crawlers, still suck.
 - Still can't have NPCs take up extra seats in vehicles.
 - The designs of the Fencer and Barga are inferior to their predecessors.

While I personally liked the story progression in 4.1 better and the localization in 5 doesn't work quite as well at times, this is still very much a silly, fun EDF game. As expected from a sequel, the maps feel bigger (and they use them better), it has some way cooler setpieces, graphics looks noticably better and they fixed the lack of proper mouse controls in the main menu that 4.1 had. I do think the songs were better in 4.1, but they are still ok here and the random NPC voice lines during missions are probably a notch better in 5. The tutorial missions (offline play only) are a neat addition and it's fun that each class gets their own origin story, if you will. I wish they would give the poor wing diver some more clothes, though.

Some of the major changes from 4.1 are that the ranger class now gets some limited vehicles, you can no longer bring two copies of the exact same weapon (unless you play fencer) and there are some other miscellaneous changes to the loadout system that I think work pretty well. Getting duplicates of weapons from the weapon crates can now help level up your weapons and make them better, so you no longer have the 4.1 experience of finding 12 duplicates in a mission and getting nothing for it.
Some of the Air Raider bombardment items now give you a zoomed out view where you can move and rotate a bombing run line so that you know pretty much exactly where it's going to land. No more wild guessing for those items :)
Clearing a level on any difficulty also counts as having cleared it on all lower difficulties, so no more need to play through Easy if you want to do everything.

Overall it's a very good EDF entry, probably better than 4.1 in most cases.
Pretty meh. Over-priced for what it is, Feels like a cheap Unity game. Don't get the price tag or the appeal.
